items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: In 1943 most of your men are in the service and then you get a letter from President Roosevelt that you were drafted.

ctx.x: time or whatever, so he started baran-bam - baran-bam; Mario start to give it a broken chord to the saxophone and him with the trumpet and then after sometime Mario create the melody on top of .....

Okay, all right, we'll get to that later. In 1943 most of your men are in the service and then you get a letter from President Roosevelt that you were drafted. Tell me about that, when you opened that mailbox in ....

In March. It was a big envelope and I was acquainted with the envelope already because Pin Madera received one, you know, so I said to myself, well, they got me. They give me fifteen days, so I worked the fifteen days because I need the money for my family; so that particular morning, Sunday morning or Monday morning, I went to Whitehall and from Whitehall we went to Camp Upton in the White area. It was a new experience altogether, I got there about six o'clock in the morning. It was drizzling, you know, it was…
